text: When we look at the skills required to do your job, by 2030, it will change by 70%. So whether or not you're looking to change your job, your job is changing.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: Lenny asks Tomer why he decided to completely rethink how product development works at LinkedIn and why other leaders need to pay attention to this transformation. Tomer explains that LinkedIn has unique visibility into the changing nature of work, and their data shows that 70% of the skills required for any given job will change by 2030. This rapid pace of change means companies must fundamentally reimagine their approach to building products to stay competitive.
text_ko: 지금 하시는 직무(job)에 필요한 역량(skills)을 보면 2030년까지 약 70%가 달라질 거예요. 그래서 이직을 하든 안 하든 여러분의 직무는 이미 변하고 있어요.
text_zh: 就技能要求来说，到2030年，你这份工作所需的技能会改变70%。所以不管你打不打算换工作，你的岗位本身都会在变。
text_es: Si analizamos las habilidades que exige tu trabajo, para 2030 habrán cambiado en un 70%. Así que, aunque no estés pensando en cambiar de empleo, tu puesto sí está cambiando.
original_text: When we look at the skills required to do your job, by 2030, it will change by 70%. So whether or not you're looking to change your job, your job is changing. In order to stay competitive, you actually have to go back to some first principles, go back to the drawing board and reimagine what it means to be building.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities or expertise that enable an individual to perform tasks effectively and efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of employment and career development, 'skills' refer to the competencies that are increasingly required in the workforce, particularly as technology and job roles evolve.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can encompass both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and its usage can vary based on the specific context of job requirements.

vocabulary.definition: The act or process of making something different, which can involve alterations in structure, function, or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'change' is often discussed in relation to organizational development, market dynamics, and the need for adaptation to remain competitive.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'change' can have a neutral connotation, it often carries a sense of urgency or necessity in business discussions, particularly in fast-paced environments.

text: We call it the full stack builder model. The goal itself is to empower great builders to take their idea and to take it to market, regardless of their role and the stack and which team they're on.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: Lenny asks Tomer to explain the name and concept of the new program LinkedIn has developed. The full stack builder model is LinkedIn's radical approach to product development that enables individual contributors to take products from idea to launch regardless of their traditional function. Unlike traditional teams where product managers, designers, and engineers work in sequence, this model creates a seamless collaboration between humans and AI tools.
text_ko: 우리는 그걸 풀스택 빌더 모델(full stack builder model)이라고 불러요. 목표는 훌륭한 빌더들이 어떤 역할을 맡고 있든, 어떤 스택(stack)을 쓰든, 어떤 팀에 속해 있든 관계없이 자신의 아이디어를 실행해 시장에 내놓을 수 있게 힘을 실어주는 거예요.
text_zh: 我们称它为“全栈构建者模型”（full stack builder model）。目标就是赋能那些优秀的实干者，把想法做出来并推向市场——不管他们是什么角色、用的是什么技术栈（stack），或者在哪个团队里。
text_es: Lo llamamos el modelo del creador full-stack (full stack builder). El objetivo es darles a los mejores creadores las herramientas para llevar su idea al mercado, sea cual sea su rol, el stack tecnológico (stack) o el equipo en el que estén.
key_sentence: The full stack builder model empowers builders to take ideas to market.
original_text: We call it the full stack builder model. The goal itself is to empower great builders to take their idea and to take it to market, regardless of their role and the stack and which team they're on. It's really fluid interaction between human and machine.

vocabulary.definition: To give someone the authority or power to do something; to enable or support individuals to take control of their own actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, empowering employees often leads to increased innovation and productivity, as individuals feel more confident in making decisions and taking initiative.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'empower' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply a shift in responsibility that may not always be welcomed by all team members.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the complete set of technologies and layers involved in software development, from front-end user interfaces to back-end databases and servers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, a 'full stack' approach allows teams to develop and manage all aspects of a product, enhancing flexibility and efficiency in development processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'full stack' implies versatility, it can also suggest a lack of specialization, which may not always be ideal for complex projects.

text: Change management here is going to be a critical part, but it's not enough to give them the tools. You have to build the incentives programs, the motivation, the examples to how you do it.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: Lenny observes that top performers are finding the most success with AI tools and asks about adoption challenges. Tomer explains that simply providing AI tools to employees isn't sufficient for organizational transformation. He emphasizes that successful adoption requires comprehensive change management including performance incentives, motivational programs, and concrete examples of success. He notes that many companies fail by just deploying AI agents without supporting the cultural shift needed for adoption.
text_ko: 여기선 변화 관리(change management)가 굉장히 중요하지만, 단지 도구만 제공하는 것으론 부족해요. 인센티브 프로그램(incentive programs), 동기 부여 장치, 그리고 실제로 어떻게 하는지 보여주는 구체적인 실행 사례를 만들어야 해요.
text_zh: 变革管理(change management)在这儿很关键，但光给大家工具不够。你得把激励机制(incentives)建起来、想办法调动积极性、树立示范，教大家具体怎么做。
text_es: Aquí la gestión del cambio (change management) va a ser clave, pero no basta con darles las herramientas. Hay que poner en marcha programas de incentivos, generar la motivación y dar ejemplos de cómo hacerlo.
key_sentence: it's not enough to give them the tools.
original_text: Change management here is going to be a critical part, but it's not enough to give them the tools. You have to build the incentives programs, the motivation, the examples to how you do it. I see a lot of companies roll out their agents and just expecting companies to adopt. It doesn't work this way.

vocabulary.definition: Change management refers to the structured approach to transitioning individuals, teams, and organizations from a current state to a desired future state.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology settings, effective change management is crucial for implementing new processes, technologies, or organizational structures while minimizing resistance and maximizing engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a systematic process that includes planning, communication, and support, and should be used when discussing formal strategies to manage transitions.

vocabulary.definition: Incentives programs are structured initiatives designed to motivate individuals or teams to achieve specific goals or behaviors through rewards or recognition.
vocabulary.businessContext: Incentives programs are commonly used in corporate environments to enhance employee performance, increase productivity, and foster loyalty by aligning individual goals with organizational objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While incentives programs can be effective, they should be carefully designed to ensure they promote desired behaviors without unintended consequences, such as unhealthy competition.

vocabulary.definition: Motivation is the internal or external drive that prompts individuals to take action towards achieving goals or fulfilling needs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, understanding employee motivation is essential for leaders to create an environment that fosters engagement, productivity, and job satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term encompasses both intrinsic and extrinsic factors, and should be used when discussing the reasons behind an individual's or team's actions.

text: Top talent has this tendency of continuously trying to get better at their craft. The key trait that I'm emphasizing for builders is where I want them to spend their time is where I think great builders should shine in.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: Lenny questions whether AI makes average people better or makes great people even better. Tomer confirms that LinkedIn's top performers are the most successful with their new AI-powered tools, explaining that high performers naturally seek to improve their craft and stay at the cutting edge. He then transitions to describing the specific traits he wants builders to focus on - vision, empathy, communication, creativity, and judgment - rather than automatable tasks.
text_ko: 최고 인재들은 자신의 실력을 계속해서 더 나아지게 하려는 경향이 있어요. 제가 빌더들(builders)에게 특히 강조하는 핵심은 그들이 시간을 어디에 쓰느냐인데, 바로 그 지점에서 훌륭한 빌더들이 빛나야 한다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 顶尖人才都有一个特点，就是会不断地想要在自己的专业领域做得更好。我特别看重做产品的人(builders)的一个品质，就是我希望他们把时间花在真正能让优秀产品人发光发热的地方。
text_es: El talento de primera tiene esa tendencia de siempre estar tratando de mejorar en lo suyo. La característica clave que les recalco a los que construyen es en qué quiero que inviertan su tiempo, ahí es donde creo que los grandes constructores realmente deben brillar.
key_sentence: Top talent continuously tries to get better at their craft and shine in.

vocabulary.definition: A tendency refers to an inclination or a habitual pattern of behavior or thought. It indicates a likelihood or predisposition towards a certain action or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding the tendencies of employees or market trends can help organizations anticipate changes and make informed strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'tendency' suggests a natural inclination, it does not imply certainty, making it important to consider context when discussing behaviors or trends.

vocabulary.definition: Emphasizing means to give special importance or prominence to something in order to highlight its significance or value. It often involves stressing particular points to ensure they are understood.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, emphasizing key messages during presentations or communications can enhance clarity and ensure that critical information is retained by the audience.
vocabulary.nuance: The act of emphasizing can convey urgency or priority, so it should be used judiciously to avoid diluting the impact of the message.

vocabulary.definition: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic or quality, especially one that forms a part of an individual's personality. Traits can be inherent or developed over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying key traits in employees can help organizations in recruitment and team dynamics, as certain traits may be more conducive to specific roles or company cultures.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'trait' often refers to positive attributes, it can also encompass negative characteristics, so context is essential when discussing traits in a professional environment.

text: We ended up building our own trust agent at LinkedIn.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: Lenny asks about the specific AI agents LinkedIn has built to automate parts of product development. Tomer explains that LinkedIn couldn't use off-the-shelf AI tools and had to build custom agents tailored to their specific needs. The trust agent is one example - it analyzes product specifications and identifies potential security vulnerabilities and harm vectors that could affect users. This agent was built by LinkedIn's head of trust and incorporates all their unique trust considerations.
text_ko: 결국 링크드인에서 저희만의 신뢰 에이전트(trust agent)를 직접 구축하게 됐어요.
text_zh: 最后我们在 LinkedIn 自己开发了一个信任代理（trust agent）。
text_es: Al final acabamos construyendo nuestro propio agente de confianza (trust agent) en LinkedIn.
key_sentence: We ended up building our own trust agent at LinkedIn.
original_text: We ended up building our own trust agent at LinkedIn. So when you build a spec, you build an idea, you walk through the trust agent and it'll basically tell you what are your vulnerabilities, what harm vectors potentially you're introducing or will be introduced as a result of that.

vocabulary.definition: An individual or system that establishes and maintains trust between parties, often by ensuring transparency and reliability in interactions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, trust agents play a vital role in building relationships with customers and stakeholders, particularly in industries where trust is paramount, such as finance and technology.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'trust agent' implies a proactive role in fostering trust, which is essential in environments where skepticism may exist; however, it should not be confused with mere compliance or regulation.

text: Whether you're in an organization, you're waiting for your leader to roll this out or you're a leader trying to roll this out, I would not wait. If you're looking for a formal reorg or declaration to start building differently, you're waiting too long.
speaker: Tomer Cohen
context: In his final advice, Lenny asks what leaders should know about implementing similar AI-powered product development changes. Tomer emphasizes urgency and personal agency rather than waiting for organizational permission. He argues that individuals should start experimenting with AI tools and adopting a full-stack builder mindset immediately, regardless of whether their company has formally announced such programs. He believes waiting for official reorganizations or declarations will put people behind in the rapidly changing landscape.
text_ko: 조직 안에서 리더가 이걸 도입(roll out)해 주길 기다리든, 리더로서 직접 도입하려 하든, 저는 기다리지 말라고 권해요. 형식적인 재편(reorg)이나 선언을 기다려서 다르게 만들어 가기 시작하려 한다면, 이미 너무 늦었어요.
text_zh: 不管你是在公司里等着领导推这个事儿，还是你就是那个要推的领导，我觉得都别等了。如果你还在等什么正式的重组或者官方声明才开始换个思路做事，那就等太久了。
text_es: Ya sea que estés en una organización esperando a que tu jefe implemente esto, o seas tú el líder tratando de implementarlo, yo no esperaría. Si estás esperando una reestructuración formal o una declaración oficial para empezar a construir de manera diferente, te estás tardando demasiado.
key_sentence: Don't wait for a formal reorg; start building differently now.
